submissions.title: Google to pay Entergy Arkansas $526 million for solar facility to feed West Memphis data center
submissions.excerpt: Google to pay Entergy Arkansas $526 million for solar facility to feed West Memphis data center
submissions.note: Tracked project 'Google West Memphis' (slug: google-west-memphis). New power-infrastructure detail: Google is paying Entergy Arkansas $526M upfront (roughly one-third of a $1.6B facility) to build 'Cypress Solar,' a 600MW solar field plus 350MW battery-storage facility that feeds the grid supplying the West Memphis data center. This is GENERATION/grid-supply capacity, not confirmed site IT load -- the tracker currently has no MW disclosed for this project at all. The $526M is Google's contribution to third-party generation infrastructure, distinct from the data center's own construction capex (currently on file as an estimated $4B through 2027) -- do not sum them. No projectId supplied: see network-access note in the companion DataVolt Oxagon submission from this same batch (tracker.bepresearch.com is blocked by this session's egress policy).

submissions.title: Docs reveal plans for $6 utility rate hike to help fund Google's data center project in West Memphis
submissions.excerpt: Docs reveal plans for $6 utility rate hike to help fund Google's data center project in West Memphis
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: utility cost-allocation dispute tied to tracked project 'Google West Memphis' (slug: google-west-memphis). Leaked Entergy/Arkansas PSC documents show residential ratepayers funding roughly two-thirds of the solar/battery buildout backing the data center via a near-$6/month bill increase. Separately and same week, a federal judge on 2026-09-02 rejected Entergy's bid to block the Arkansas Democrat-Gazette from publishing the underlying contract documents (companion coverage: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/02/google-data-center-arkansas-entergy-court.html -- not submitted as its own candidate to avoid a near-duplicate URL, but worth a human read alongside this one). Illustrates the ratepayer cost-shifting and contract-confidentiality fights increasingly attached to hyperscaler power deals; relevant to the tracker's utility-connection-rules category even though nothing here changes the project's own MW/capex figures. No projectId supplied -- see network-access note in the DataVolt Oxagon submission from this batch.

submissions.title: Vantage data center gets zone change OK from Laramie County Tuesday
submissions.excerpt: an investment of up to $20 billion when it's completed
submissions.note: NEW PROJECT candidate -- checked against the current data/projects.json export (103 projects) and found no existing Wyoming/Laramie County entry, so this looks untracked. Laramie County commissioners approved a zone change (Land Use to Planned Unit Development) on 2026-09-01 for Vantage Data Centers' 'Project Latigo,' a proposed data center on ~1,835 acres about 12 miles south of Cheyenne, WY. Reported: 480MW initial build with potential to scale toward ~1GW, investment up to $20B (initial phase estimated $4.8-9.6B), on-site natural gas generation, closed-loop cooling, construction targeted to start 2027. Early-stage (zoning approval only, no groundbreaking yet) but crosses the >=$1B / >=100MW threshold. IT-load vs. site-power basis not yet disclosed by the company. submissions.title: Thailand Puts 49 Data Centers on Hold Over Resource Strain
submissions.excerpt: Thailand Puts 49 Data Centers on Hold Over Resource Strain
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION, country-level, not tied to a single tracked project. Thailand's National Economic and Social Development Council (NESDC) asked 49 data-center projects nationwide to voluntarily pause construction amid public concern over power and resource strain, pending new industry regulations the government says are expected within about a month; NESDC secretary-general Danucha Pichayanan is reported (per AFP, via Bloomberg/SCMP/w.media coverage) as saying the state has no legal authority to force a halt -- this is a request for cooperation, not a binding moratorium, and the review queue should record that distinction rather than 'ban.' Context: Thailand approved 88 AI/data-center projects worth ~886B baht (~US$27B) in H1 2026, already surpassing all of 2025, so this is a sudden brake on a fast-growing pipeline. CAVEAT: WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for bloomberg.com (and every other outlet tried) this session, so the excerpt is the verbatim article headline as returned by search rather than a body-text quote -- please verify the body text at the link.
